stance.label: Taiwan near its bear line · selling eases · stay on plan

headline: Taiwan drops 948 points, dips below 40,000 then recovers; foreign selling halves; Nvidia reports tonight
summary: Taiwan took a second leg down today, but the selling is easing: the TAIEX fell 2.3%, and foreign net selling was about half of yesterday's. The index is only 0.6% above its bear line, yet by the rules it is still a correction in an uptrend, with only 1 systemic light on. Nvidia's results after the US close tonight decide whether chips can steady. Keep regular investing on plan.

overview.lead: Taiwan fell less than yesterday, and it sold off first and then bounced: the TAIEX lost 2.3%, closing about 300 points above its intraday low.
points: The TAIEX briefly broke below 40,000 intraday and closed at 40,092.
TSMC (2330) fell 2% to NT$2,170, a third of yesterday's drop.
MediaTek (2454) rose 1.2%, one of the few large caps to rise.
Selling moved to smaller tech names: the OTC index fell 3.9%, more than the TAIEX.
400 stocks rose and 1,449 fell, so decliners still dominated.

focus.lead: Among the nine tracked, the Taiwan names are under the most strain: 0050 broke its 200-day line, and the two Taiwan funds' NAVs have yet to reflect today's drop.
points: 0050 fell 2.5%, slipping from above its 200-day line to below it.
0050 is −19.3% from its high, with tier 5 still 13.2% away; the framework has no new action.
Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8) each fell about 8% on their 11/16 NAVs; all tiers are used.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan (TW000T5011A9) NAV only runs to 11/13, so it has not reflected Taiwan's two down days this week.
SPY and QQQ stay at their 11/16 closes; Nvidia's results tonight are the next swing factor.

position.lead: No new tier was hit today; the closest is still QQQ tier 3, 2.4% away.
points: QQQ has hit two tiers; tier 3 at 645.71 is 2.4% away.
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) NAV fell 3.7% on 11/16, cutting the gap to tier 5 to 7.5%.
SPY tier 2 at 701.18 is 5.2% away.
0050 tier 5 at 81.55 is 13.2% away.
Allianz Taiwan Technology and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend have used all tiers; further NAV drops trigger nothing new.

macro.lead: Taiwan's outside pressure today came from the currency: a strong dollar pushed the NT dollar past 33 intraday.
points: The NT dollar weakened to 33.015 intraday, a year-and-a-half low.
The US 10-year yield is 5.12% (11/16); long rates still weigh on tech valuations.
The high-yield spread is 3.2% (11/13); credit markets remain calm.
US October retail sales come out tonight at 21:30 Taipei; a strong print would push rates up again.

sentiment.lead: Taiwan sentiment looks like the late stage of a flush: margin debt is down nearly a fifth, and new lows far outnumber new highs.
points: Margin balances fell 18.9% over 20 days; the deleveraging signal is on.
Only 19% of stocks are above their 200-day line; the breadth-collapse light is on.
196 new lows versus 5 new highs; the decline has spread across the market.
CNN Fear & Greed is at 30, in fear but not extreme fear.

sectors.lead: Today's rotation was clear: electronic components kept falling, while financials, telecom and food were the shelters.
points: Electronic components fell 6.9% and are down over 30% in a month.
Cooling maker AVC (3017) fell 9.9% and Delta Electronics (2308) fell 5.8%; the AI supply chain is still the epicenter.
Cathay Financial (2882) and CTBC Financial (2891) rose 0.9% each, and Chunghwa Telecom (2412) rose 0.6%.
Local funds bought Formosa Chemicals, Formosa Plastics and financials, shifting toward low-valuation and defensive names.

taiwan.lead: Institutional selling eased clearly today, but foreigners have not stopped: foreign net selling was NT$38.1B, just over half of yesterday's.
points: The three institutional groups sold a net NT$54.7B, versus NT$114.4B the day before.
Foreign 20-day net selling totals NT$1.14 trillion; the outflow is still large.
Local investment trusts sold a small NT$0.9B, ending a 24-day buying streak.
Foreign net short TAIEX futures stand at 97,896 contracts, up 1,109; only a small addition.
November TAIEX futures settle tomorrow; volatility often widens around settlement.

watch.lead: Three hurdles in the next 48 hours: retail sales tonight, Nvidia results early tomorrow, and futures settlement tomorrow.
points: US October retail sales at 21:30 Taipei on 11/17.
Nvidia reports after the US close on 11/17, early 11/18 Taipei; it decides whether chips can steady.
November TAIEX futures settle on 11/18.
FOMC October minutes early 11/19 Taipei.
TAIEX bear line at 39,858, only 0.6% away.

regime.lead: By the rules, Taiwan is still a correction in an uptrend, not a turn bearish: the 200-day line is still rising and only 1 systemic light is on.
points: Trend: the TAIEX has closed below its 200-day line 2 days running, 3.2% under, and the line is still rising.
Systemic lights: Taiwan has 1 on (breadth collapse); credit, the economy and financial conditions show no trouble yet.
The closest global light is the S&P 500 breaking its 200-day line, only 1% away.
Capitulation signals: Taiwan has 3 on — margin deleveraging, breadth washout, and a surge in new lows.
History: when Taiwan fell this far, it usually went on past −20%; all 10 past episodes did.
Only 3 episodes fell this fast, and all 3 broke −20%; the sample is too small, use as reference only.
What would flip the view: 5 closes below 41,428 with a flattening 200-day line means weak.
A close below 39,858 meets the bear-market definition; 3 systemic lights would shift the call to possibly bearish.
